bull.b: Sustained gross margins near 75.8% indicate attractive unit economics for neffy. As prescription volumes and refill rates scale, these margins can translate into durable operating leverage, making the business more likely to generate operating profits once SG&A and commercialization spending normalize.

Rapid prescription growth, a growing installed base (~120k patients) and expanded field force (148 reps) reflect durable market penetration. Repeat prescribing (~50% repeat HCP use) and school program deployments build stickiness, supporting sustainable refill-driven revenue over multiple years.

Label changes and approvals in Canada and the EU materially enlarge the addressable market and enable partner-led launches (e.g., ALK). Regulatory wins and pediatric label expansion are structural, allowing multi-region commercialization and revenue diversification over the medium term.

bear.b: Sustained negative operating and free cash flow (~-$175M TTM) creates ongoing funding needs. Even with ~$201M on hand, the company faces financing risk if commercialization ramps or SG&A remains elevated; reliance on future breakeven timing increases execution and dilution risk.

Deep, persistent net losses and an SG&A base well ahead of revenue create structural profitability hurdles. Returns on equity are negative and equity has fallen, reducing balance-sheet resilience and meaningfully raising the bar for sustained profitable scale without further cost control or sizable revenue expansion.

High prior-authorization incidence, elevated abandonment and a ~50% gross-to-net materially limit realized revenue and retention. These payer-driven structural barriers can cap uptake, compress margins, and make growth timing dependent on favorable payer decisions and durable formulary placements.
